purpose: improve the speed or resource use of a running system against a stated target, and keep the gain from regressing
entry_criteria: A target exists, such as p95 latency or cost per request
A repeatable load or benchmark exists
procedure: Reproduce the problem with a benchmark whose result you trust, and record the baseline with its spread.
Locate the bottleneck with profiles and traces; list the top three causes by time share.
Change one thing at a time, starting with the largest share, and re-measure after each change.
Keep only changes that improve the target beyond the noise; revert the rest.
Check that the gain holds on production-like data and does not move cost or errors elsewhere.
Add a performance check to CI or monitoring so a regression is caught, and record what was learned.
deliverables: list of kept and reverted changes
acceptance_criteria: Target met or the shortfall is explained
Each kept change has measured benefit
validation_method: Performance engineer and service owner review.

validation.check: run the same benchmark three times before and after and compare the medians

validation.expect: all functional tests pass after the changes

failure_modes.response: Add the CI or alert check

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A search endpoint has p95 of 1.2 s against a 500 ms target. A profile shows 60 percent in one N+1 query; batching it brings p95 to 450 ms, and a latency alert is added at 600 ms.
